objectClass.primaryType: architectural complex (university library building: central domed hall, symmetric brick wings, twin corner towers, axial plaza with pool)
objectClass.notes: Symmetric bilateral complex around a central axis (forward +Z toward the plaza). Front face = 5-storey wings (terracotta brick, cream string courses, barrel-tile hip roofs) ending in square belfry towers with pyramid roofs; centre = tall glazed loggia behind a columned portico, glass dome with cream drum above; two low front pavilions flank the portico; rear wings extend north closing a courtyard with glazed vault gallery and a sloped glass canopy (report hall) at the west nook. Foreground plaza: grand steps, turf parterre with dark hedge blocks, scalloped-edge pool with two stepped circular fountains, plane-tree rows. Inference, not measurement: exact north (rear) plan depths and courtyard details are inferred from aerials (ref-02/ref-04); rear facades assumed to continue the front rhythm.

reasoning: Silhouette is heavily interrupted: dome + drum above the central glazed attic, two tall towers with pyramid caps, hip-roofed wings and pavilions, all read against the sky in the elevation view.
Hundreds of visible sub-parts: window grids on both wings (approx 5 floors x 14 bays per wing), pilaster strips, string courses, roof ridges, drum windows, colonnade, balustrades.
Deep hierarchy: root > wing > body/roof > window-grid repetition > frame/glass/sill micro features; every macro mass carries 3+ levels.
Repetition density is high and regular (brick courses, tile ribs, windows, dentils, balusters, tree rows, hedge blocks) — the building's identity IS its rhythm.

Materials: terracotta brick, cream limestone trim, olive stone piers/columns, two glazing systems (dark curtain glass, blue-grey dome glass), barrel tile, granite paving/step stone, pool water, foliage — 8+ distinct responses.
Local detail density is moderate per surface but the repeated systems make small errors (wrong window pitch, missing dentils) highly visible at the review distance.
Occlusion: single views hide the rear plan; the 4 supplied views cover the front, both aerials and a rear-quarter, so rear massing is inferable but reported as inference.
Action readiness: static architectural prop; needs clickable/explodable part tree for the demo but no skeletal animation.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Architectural complex with dense repeated systems and many materials: fidelity depends on deep hierarchy (root > block > assembly > feature) and repetition systems for windows, columns, ridges and planting. Ultra-complex floors (5 macro / 16 meso / 8 micro / 4 material layers / 2 repetition systems / 5 viewpoints) are the correct bar.

detailInventory.note: Full descriptions and per-image regions live in assessment.json; refs below point at the authored feature/override ids.

referenceSuitability.rationale: Four views cover the front elevation, front 3/4 aerial, close aerial (roof/massing) and rear-quarter aerial. Front photos show a strong silhouette and every major material. This is an architectural scene rather than a single isolated object, but the building is an unambiguous single target occupying the frame centre; hidden sides are inferable from the aerial views and are reported as inference. Exact photo-projection is not applicable (no surface pattern worth projecting at this scale); material evidence extraction applies for palette/scalars.

definitionOfDone: From the plaza (ref-03 alignment) the silhouette reads as the same building: central glazed loggia + dome above, two symmetric 5-storey wings ending in belfry towers with pyramid caps, low pavilions flanking the entrance, wide steps to the terrace.
Window rhythm is legible and regular on both wings (no missing/extra bays, floor lines continuous); towers carry the paired-slot windows and belfry arches.

Roofscape matches the aerials: hip roofs with pale ridge caps on wings/pavilions/towers, flat central deck with dome + drum + equipment cluster (solar row, AC boxes, low skylights), courtyard glass vault and sloped glass canopy present.

Plaza stage matches ref-01/ref-03: turf parterre with dark hedge blocks on the axis, scalloped pool with two stepped circular fountains, tree rows, warm granite paving; steps and terrace balustrade on the central axis.

Materials are reference-derived: two glazing systems (dark curtain glass, blue-grey dome glass), terracotta brick with subtle per-bay variation, pale limestone trim/string courses/cornices, olive-tan portico columns, barrel-tile roofs with rib pattern, water with glass sheen — each with independent roughness/response.
Clickable/explodable part tree: every named component is addressable via sculptRuntime; no orphan meshes; symmetric pairs mirror exactly.
All six review viewpoints (front, front-high 3/4, close aerial, rear 3/4, left, right) hold the structure without broken silhouettes or floating parts.

featureGroups.name: Central glazed loggia + dome
qualityCriteria: Loggia glass band divided by olive piers into the same bay count as the reference, with transom lines; dark glass with sky sheen.
Dome sits on a cream drum with a continuous window ribbon; dome shell shows the pane grid + meridian/ring ribs; apex cap present.
Dentil attic band between loggia top and parapet; dome reads clearly above the ridge line from the plaza.
failureModes: dome too small/large or swallowed behind the parapet in the elevation
loggia reads as solid wall instead of a glazed band
drum without window ribbon or dome without grid pattern

featureGroups.name: Symmetric wing facades
qualityCriteria: Regular window grid (bay pitch constant, floor lines continuous), recessed reveals with sills, pilaster strips between bays.
Cream string courses at each floor line and eave cornice with dentils.
Wings mirror each other exactly (reflection, not rotation).
failureModes: window pitch drifts across the facade

featureGroups.name: Twin corner towers
qualityCriteria: Square shaft with cream front panel carrying stacked narrow paired windows; arched belfry stage with cream surrounds; balustrade row; shallow hip/pyramid roof with ridge cap and finial.
Towers rise clearly above the wings in the elevation silhouette; tower top reads open (arch shadows), not solid.
failureModes: tower reads as a plain brick box (no cream panel/slots/arches)
tower height lost against the wing
pyramid roof wrong pitch or missing

featureGroups.name: Entrance portico, terrace and grand steps
qualityCriteria: Columned portico on the central axis with entablature slab, recessed glazed wall with red banners behind.
Three wide flights of steps between plaza and terrace with pale nosing lines and landing bands; terrace balustrade segments on both sides.
Portico reads in front of the loggia with correct depth when seen from the plaza (ref-03) and from above (ref-04).
failureModes: portico merged into the facade with no depth
steps missing or replaced by a single ramp

featureGroups.name: Roofscape and courtyard glazing (aerial match)
qualityCriteria: Hip roofs with tile rib pattern and pale ridge caps on wings, pavilions and towers; correct hip slopes.
Central flat deck with dome + drum, solar panel row, AC boxes, low skylight strips; parapet with coping line.
Courtyard contains the ribbed glass barrel vault gallery and the sloped framed glass canopy at the west nook.
failureModes: glass vault/canopy missing so the courtyard loses its glass identity

featureGroups.name: Axial plaza with pool and parterre
qualityCriteria: Parterre on axis: turf strips with dark hedge blocks in rows, bounded by pale paving.
Pool basin with scalloped pale coping and two stepped circular fountains on axis, turquoise water with sheen.
Plane-tree rows frame the plaza; paving tones warm grey-beige matching ref-03.
failureModes: parterre missing so the axis reads empty
water reads flat grey instead of turquoise with sheen

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

observations: Symmetric facade: 5-storey brick halls each side, terminal towers, central glazed loggia with dome behind.
Portico of eight olive columns in front of a recessed dark glass wall; wide stepped terrace down to the plaza.
Foreground: turf parterre with dark hedge blocks, large scalloped pool with two stepped circular fountains.
Materials: terracotta brick, cream trim bands, dark glazing, terracotta tile roofs.
Whole composition with plaza, pools, tree rows and steps visible at golden hour.
Tower tips and dome read against the sky; hip roofs visible behind the parapets.
Dome: glass pane grid on a cream drum with window ribbon; solar panel row and AC boxes on the flat deck.
Courtyard: sloped framed glass canopy in the west nook; ribbed barrel vault bridging to the east block.
Hip roofs with pale ridge caps; windows in regular rows with cream frames and sills.
Building massing from the rear confirms the symmetric U with the dome toward the front half.
City and hills beyond: excluded from the model scope.

acceptance: Silhouette reads correctly without materials.
Quality contract has named all required macro feature groups before code generation.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Build the component hierarchy implied by the pre-spec complexity assessment.
acceptance: Macro, meso, and repeated structures meet qualityContract.minimumSpecDepth.
Parent-child relations, joints, seams, sockets, and contact points are explicit.
Every attached child appendage/connector has parentSocket, localStart/localEnd, contactType, embedDepth or overlap, and gapTolerance.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Refine shape, deformation, bevels, tapers, curves, asymmetry, and visible local geometry.
acceptance: Important visible forms are represented in component geometryDescriptor, deformations, localFeatures, or repetitionSystems.
Endpoint-based child parts are rooted at their attachment sockets and do not visibly float away from parents.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Add procedural surface locality such as normal/bump, AO, dirt, stains and wear.
acceptance: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.
A grazing-angle close-up proves that normal/height detail breaks highlights naturally and does not read as smooth plastic.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral and reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.
Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make every named part clickable and explodable from one part definition.
acceptance: Macro and movable meso components have stable pivot nodes.
Sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata are present for future runtime actions.
Click and explode resolve to the same part list (check_part_coverage manifest).

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Reach accepted visual fidelity first, then optimize without removing reference-critical geometry or surface layers.

lightingFromPhoto: key light: warm low sun from the front-west quarter (ref-01 golden hour); color #FFD9A0, relative intensity 2.6; in the neutral preview a high sun at (-70, 80, 60) aims at the plaza axis
fill light: cool sky dome fill (hemisphere), color #BFD4E8 over ground #3A3A3A, relative intensity 0.55
rim or environment light: soft sky environment reflection for the glazing and dome (RoomEnvironment via PMREM), envMapIntensity 0.8; weak warm back rim at (10, 45, -90)
exposure and tone mapping: ACESFilmic tone mapping, exposure 1.0, background gradient from pale blue zenith to warm horizon haze
contact shadow: PCFSoft directional shadow at ~35 deg sun elevation, 4096 map; ground contact shadows under trees, halls, towers and pool coping; per-material AO darkens seams and recesses
reference note: ref-03 is high noon (hard cold key, deep blue sky) while ref-01/ref-04 are golden hour; previews standardize on a late-afternoon warm key for comparison against ref-01/ref-03
proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
animationAnchors: root pivot node supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale, and visibility changes

destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
risks: Repetition emitters in the generator handle radial arrays only; linear grids (windows, columns, trees, hedges) are documented in repetitionSystems and implemented by code loops in the factory (refine-code).
Hip roofs and arch openings need small factory helpers (custom geometry) beyond stock primitives.
Fidelity depends on keeping the window pitch and floor lines exact; a wrong pitch is highly visible at review distance.
